name: Aaron and Miriam
charge: Speaking against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman, and claiming an equal standing: hath he not spoken also by us?
summary: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman, who was Zipporah the daughter of the priest of Midian, whom the Lord had allowed him. The woman was the excuse; what they actually said was a claim of equal standing with the man God had set over them, and the Lord heard it. He came down and declared the difference to their faces, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow: a father’s spit in her face, seven days without the camp, while the whole nation waited.
offenseFull: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman he had married (Numbers 12:1). This is still Zipporah, the daughter of the priest of Midian, whom Moses married in the forty years he dwelt outside Egypt, when he was in a land by himself with none of his own people around him, and whom the Lord allowed him (Exodus 2:16, 21); a place being called Midian and the woman being called an Ethiopian is no contradiction. They had said nothing about her when Moses was saving them out of Egypt, nor when he set Aaron over the men and Miriam over the women; the murmuring came from somewhere else and they took hold of what was at hand.

The woman was the excuse. The charge is what they actually said: they asked whether the Lord had spoken only by Moses, and not also by them, and the Lord heard it (Numbers 12:2). Was the Most High dealing with Aaron and Miriam? He was. He was dealing with Moses more, and that is what could not be borne, so the real matter was a covetousness for his standing dressed up as a complaint about his wife. The teaching names the pattern: a man who has a problem with the leadership goes looking for something in the leadership to hold up, so that when he gossips and murmurs about the body he looks like the righteous one; pull the curtain back and it was never about the thing he named, it was about power. The man Moses was very meek, above all the men on the face of the earth (Numbers 12:3), so this was no hard man provoking them. Those who despise government are presumptuous and selfwilled, and are not afraid to speak evil of dignities (2 Peter 2:10).
judgmentFull: The Lord spoke suddenly to Moses, Aaron and Miriam, calling the three of them out to the tabernacle; He came down in the pillar of the cloud, called Aaron and Miriam forward, and declared the difference: to a prophet among them He would make Himself known in a vision and speak in a dream, but His servant Moses was not so, being faithful in all His house; with him He spoke mouth to mouth, plainly and not in dark speeches; so why were they not afraid to speak against His servant Moses (Numbers 12:4-5, 6-10). He had to let them know that He does not deal with everyone the same. They were a prophet and a prophetess and He spoke with them, but in visions and dreams; some spirits are greater than others, and a nation has to learn to accept it. The anger of the Lord was kindled, the cloud departed from the tabernacle, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow. Aaron pleaded that the sin not be laid on them, and Moses cried to the Lord to heal her (Numbers 12:11, 13-15).

The Lord answered that if her father had only spat in her face she would have been ashamed seven days, so she was to be shut out of the camp seven days and then received in again. The spit is correction, a father putting his child in her place; had she been raised to respect the men of the Lord, this would not have come on her. Miriam was shut out, and the people did not journey until she was brought in again: a whole nation held in place over one tongue. This is a charge to raise the children in the fear of the Lord and teach them to respect the elders and the men of the Lord. Children are to obey their parents in the Lord, and fathers are not to provoke their children to wrath but to bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord (Ephesians 6:1-4); parents who let their children speak evil to the men of the Lord bring the judgment on their own household. Moses made it a standing warning: Israel was to remember what the Lord their God did to Miriam by the way (Deuteronomy 24:9).

text.text: And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman.
And they said, Hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the Lord heard it.
Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.
And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.
(Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.)
But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.
And the Lord spake suddenly unto Moses, and unto Aaron, and unto Miriam, Come out ye three unto the tabernacle of the congregation. And they three came out.
And the Lord came down in the pillar of the cloud, and stood in the door of the tabernacle, and called Aaron and Miriam: and they both came forth.
And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.
My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.
With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
And the anger of the Lord was kindled against them; and he departed.
And the cloud departed from off the tabernacle; and, behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous.
And Aaron said unto Moses, Alas, my lord, I beseech thee, lay not the sin upon us, wherein we have done foolishly, and wherein we have sinned.
And Moses cried unto the Lord, saying, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee.
And the Lord said unto Moses, If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in again.
And Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days: and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again.
Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.
Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)
That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.
And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt.
